content.text: There is a new API for a new Trails backend in entire-api. The current CLI implementation still points at the BFF. Going forward we do want to point to entire-api instead. Make yourself a picture ../entire-api and implement the current trail related commands against the new API/backend.

input.command: entire agent-help

result.output:
Entire's CLI is the source of truth for its own usage. Do not guess flags or
subcommands — read them from this command. You are already inside the repo:
entire auto-detects it from the git origin remote, so never ask the user for the
repo name. Pass --repo only to target a DIFFERENT repo.

Current repo: gh/entireio/cli  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

When to use entire:
  activity     Show your activity overview
  agent        Manage agent integrations (add, remove, list)
  api          Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
  auth         Manage authentication
  blame        Show which lines came from Entire checkpoints
  checkpoint   Inspect and search checkpoints
  clean        Clean up Entire session data
  configure    Update Entire settings in the current repository
  disable      Disable Entire in current repository
  dispatch     Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work
  doctor       Diagnose and fix session issues
  enable       Enable Entire in current repository
  experts      Rank agent provenance for code scopes
  grant        Manage Entire access grants and org membership
  import       Import pre-existing agent history into Entire (experimental)
  investigate  Run a multi-agent investigation against the current branch
  labs         Explore experimental Entire workflows
  login        Log in to Entire
  logout       Log out of Entire
  org          Manage Entire organizations
  plugin       Manage Entire plugins (install, list, remove)
  project      Manage Entire projects
  recap        Summarize recent checkpoint activity
  repo         Manage Entire repositories
  review       Run a multi-agent review against the current branch
  runner       Set up and tune trail runners for this repository
  search       Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
  session      Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire
  status       Show Entire status
  tokens       Analyze token usage across sessions and checkpoints
  trail        Manage trails for your branches
  version      Show build information
  why          Show why a line exists

Drill in for exact, currently-installed flags:  entire agent-help <command>  (e.g. entire agent-help trail)
Add --json for structured output.

result.output:
entire why — Show why a line exists
Explain the commit, checkpoint, prompt, and session behind a file or line.

Target a specific line with <file>:12 or the --line flag.

Examples:
entire why src/auth.go:42
  entire why src/auth.go:42 --json

Current repo: gh/entireio/cli  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --json          Output explanation as JSON
      --line string   Explain a specific line, for example 12 (same as <file>:12)

--- checkpoint ---
entire checkpoint — Inspect and search checkpoints
Operations on checkpoints — the persistent records of agent work tied to commits.

Commands:
  list     List checkpoints on the current branch
  explain  Explain a checkpoint, commit, or session
  tokens   Show token usage and optimization recommendations
  search   Search checkpoints (semantic + keyword)

Examples:
  entire checkpoint list
  entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>
  entire checkpoint tokens <id>
  entire checkpoint search "fix login"

Current repo: gh/entireio/cli  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Subcommands: explain · list · policy · search · tokens
Next:  entire agent-help checkpoint <subcommand>

- Routes trail commands to the repository’s owning entire-api cell.
- Migrates trail, review, finding, approval, thread, resume, and SSE contracts to native camelCase responses and numbered routes.
- Supports entire-api cursor pagination.
- Handles native `204 No Content` deletes.
- Preserves compatibility with legacy snake_case payloads.
- Returns an explicit error for labels, which the new backend does not support.

- `go test ./...`

input.command:
cd ../entire.io
branch="e2e/cli-entire-api-$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
title="CLI entire-api branch E2E $(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
number=""
cleanup() {
  set +e
  if [ -n "$number" ]; then /tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail delete "$number" --force >/tmp/trail-e2e-delete.log 2>&1; cat /tmp/trail-e2e-delete.log; fi
  git push --no-verify origin --delete "$branch" >/tmp/trail-e2e-push-delete.log 2>&1 || true
  cat /tmp/trail-e2e-push-delete.log
  git branch -D "$branch" >/tmp/trail-e2e-branch-delete.log 2>&1 || true
  cat /tmp/trail-e2e-branch-delete.log
}
trap cleanup EXIT

git branch "$branch" HEAD
create_output=$(/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail create --branch "$branch" --title "$title" --body "Temporary branch-backed production smoke test." --base main --type task --priority none)
printf '%s\n' "$create_output"
number=$(printf '%s\n' "$create_output" | perl -ne 'print "$1\n" if m{/trails/(\d+)}' | tail -1)
test -n "$number"
printf '\n--- update #%s ---\n' "$number"
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail update --branch "$branch" --title "$title updated" --priority low --add-reviewer dipree
printf '\n--- show updated ---\n'
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail show "$number"

printf '\n--- create thread ---\n'
thread_json=$(/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail comment add --trail "$number" --title "CLI E2E thread" --body "Temporary thread message" --json)
printf '%s\n' "$thread_json"
thread_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$thread_json" | jq -r '.thread.id')
message_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$thread_json" | jq -r '.message.id')
test -n "$thread_id" && test "$thread_id" != null
test -n "$message_id" && test "$message_id" != null
printf '\n--- thread list/show ---\n'
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail comment list --trail "$number" --json
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail comment show --trail "$number" "$thread_id"
printf '\n--- edit and resolve thread ---\n'
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail comment edit --trail "$number" "$thread_id" "$message_id" --body "Temporary edited thread message"
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail comment resolve --trail "$number" "$thread_id"

printf '\n--- approve and list ---\n'
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail approve "$number" --message "Temporary CLI entire-api E2E approval"
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail approvals "$number" --json

printf '\n--- create/list finding ---\n'
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail finding add --trail "$number" --body "Temporary CLI entire-api E2E finding" --severity low --client-id "cli-e2e-$number" --json
/tmp/entire-trails-e2e trail finding list --trail "$number" --status any --freshness any --include-dismissed --json

printf '\nE2E_BRANCH=%s E2E_TRAIL_NUMBER=%s\n' "$branch" "$number"

content.text: How can we best keep both implementations, default to legacy for now but allow to switch?

Best approach: keep one command/domain implementation and put the backend differences behind an adapter.

### Switch

Add an explicit selector:

```bash
ENTIRE_TRAILS_BACKEND=legacy entire trail list
ENTIRE_TRAILS_BACKEND=entire-api entire trail list
```

Default to `legacy`. Optionally add a hidden persistent flag:

```bash
entire trail --backend entire-api list
```

Precedence: flag → environment → `legacy`. Don’t use automatic fallback, especially for writes, because retries could duplicate mutations.

### Backend interface

Introduce a `trailBackend` abstraction responsible for:

- Authentication/client construction
- List pagination and filtering
- Host/owner/repo/number versus trail-ID paths
- Request casing
- Response envelopes
- Delete semantics (`{ok:true}` versus `204`)
- Review, thread, approval, finding, and SSE paths

The Cobra commands should only consume canonical CLI models.

```go
type trailBackend interface {
    List(ctx context.Context, repo trailRepo, opts listOptions) (trailPage, error)
    Get(ctx context.Context, repo trailRepo, number int) (trailResource, error)
    Create(ctx context.Context, repo trailRepo, req createRequest) (trailResource, error)
    Update(ctx context.Context, repo trailRepo, number int, req updateRequest) error
    Delete(ctx context.Context, repo trailRepo, number int) error

    ReviewPath(repo trailRepo, trail trailResource) string
    ThreadPath(repo trailRepo, trail trailResource) string
    EventsPath(repo trailRepo, trail trailResource) string
}
```

Implement:

- `legacyTrailBackend`: `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient`, snake_case, limit/offset, trail-ID review routes.
- `entireAPITrailBackend`: owning-cell client, camelCase, page tokens, numbered routes.

### Important details

- Use distinct request DTOs. Compatibility decoding can accept both response formats, but writes cannot share JSON tags safely.
- Include backend mode in the trail-enablement cache key to prevent one backend’s result contaminating the other.
- Ensure non-Cobra callers such as review posting, runner gathering, resume, and background enablement refresh use the same selector.
- Keep production E2E tests for both modes and shared behavior tests that run against two mock backend contracts.

I would amend PR #1949 to introduce this adapter and make `legacy` the default, with `ENTIRE_TRAILS_BACKEND=entire-api` enabling the new implementation.
Normal commits please. Sounds like a reasonable plan, let's do it.

# Default: legacy BFF

content.text:
Implemented and pushed in commit `c66b01729`.

- Legacy BFF is the default.
- Opt into the new backend with:

```bash
ENTIRE_TRAILS_BACKEND=entire-api entire trail list
```

- Backend-specific request casing, pagination, review paths, deletion responses, and enablement cache scopes are handled independently.
- No automatic fallback for safety on writes.
- Production-tested both default legacy and entire-api opt-in flows.

PR #1949 has been updated: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1949

Entire Trail review comment
ID: 019ff135-c403-7314-8799-bf007be025d1
URL: https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1008/migrate-trail-commands-to-entire-api
Severity: medium
Context: cmd/entire/cli/api/trails.go:15
Selected context:
```
if c.TrailBackend() == "legacy" {
```
`TrailsEnabled` now defaults to the entire-api `pageSize=1` query unless the client was explicitly tagged with `WithTrailBackend("legacy")`. But `setup.go`'s enable-report probe and `agent_help_cmd.go`'s `refreshAgentHelpTrailsEnabledCacheIfStaleForScope` both build their client via plain `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient` (untagged) and still hit the legacy BFF exclusively — they never call `newTrailAPIClient`/`WithTrailBackend`. Before this change these call sites always sent `limit=1`; now they silently send `pageSize=1` to the legacy endpoint instead, which is a behavior change these callers weren't updated for.

content.text:
Fixed in `3297a84e5` and pushed.

`TrailsEnabled` now treats untagged clients as legacy:

- Untagged/legacy: `limit=1`
- Explicit `entire-api`: `pageSize=1`

Added coverage for all three cases. Targeted tests and Go lint pass.

Entire Trail review comment
ID: 019ff13e-2d28-7eb3-a400-dd541794f44a
URL: https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1008/migrate-trail-commands-to-entire-api
Severity: medium
Context: cmd/entire/cli/trail_review_cmd.go:534
Selected context:
```
client.SetTrailRoute(found.ID, trailNumberPath(host, owner, repo, found.Number))
```
`resolveTrailReviewTarget` now routes ID-keyed review/finding requests to the entire-api cell via `SetTrailRoute`, but `trailReviewCommentsPath` and `trailReviewStatePath` still build query strings with the legacy snake_case keys (`include_dismissed`, `limit`, `offset`) instead of the camelCase/cursor convention used elsewhere in this migration (e.g. `trailListPageQuery`'s `pageSize`/`pageToken`, and the `TrailsEnabled` backend-aware query fix in this same branch). If entire-api's findings endpoint expects the same camelCase convention, `entire trail finding list`, `entire trail resume`, and `runner_gather`'s trail-context gathering would silently drop the dismissed-filter and could loop forever in `fetchAllTrailReviewComments` if the server ignores `offset` and keeps returning `hasMore=true`.

package api

import "time"

// TrailReviewStateResponse is returned by GET /api/v1/trails/{trail_id}/reviews/{id}.
type TrailReviewStateResponse struct {
	Review      TrailReview            `json:"review"`
	CodeVersion TrailReviewCodeVersion `json:"codeVersion"`
	Counts      TrailReviewCounts      `json:"counts"`
	Comments    []TrailReviewComment   `json:"comments"`
	NextCursor  *string                `json:"nextCursor"`
	EventCursor string                 `json:"eventCursor"`
}

func (r *TrailReviewStateResponse) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
	type plain TrailReviewStateResponse
	return decodeNormalizedTrailJSON(data, (*plain)(r))
}

// TrailReview represents a review session.
type TrailReview struct {
	ID            string    `json:"id"`
	TrailID       string    `json:"trailId"`
	CodeVersionID string    `json:"codeVersionId"`
	ActorID       string    `json:"actorId"`
	Summary       *string   `json:"summary"`
	StartedAt     time.Time `json:"startedAt"`
}

// TrailReviewCodeVersion pins the base/head that a review covers.
type TrailReviewCodeVersion struct {
	ID           string    `json:"id"`
	TrailID      string    `json:"trailId"`
	RepositoryID string    `json:"repositoryId"`
	BaseRef      *string   `json:"baseRef"`
	HeadRef      *string   `json:"headRef"`
	BaseSHA      *string   `json:"baseSha"`
	HeadSHA      *string   `json:"headSha"`
	CapturedAt   time.Time `json:"capturedAt"`
}

// TrailReviewCounts are review-scoped comment counts.
type TrailReviewCounts struct {
	Open      int `json:"open"`
	Resolved  int `json:"resolved"`
	Dismissed int `json:"dismissed"`
	Stale     int `json:"stale"`
	Total     int `json:"total"`
}

// TrailReviewCommentsResponse is returned by trail/review comment list endpoints.
type TrailReviewCommentsResponse struct {
	Comments    []TrailReviewComment `json:"comments"`
	HasMore     bool                 `json:"hasMore"`
	NextOffset  *int                 `json:"nextOffset"`
	EventCursor string               `json:"eventCursor,omitempty"`
}

func (r *TrailReviewCommentsResponse) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
	type plain TrailReviewCommentsResponse
	return decodeNormalizedTrailJSON(data, (*plain)(r))
}

// TrailReviewComment is a single agent-native review finding.
type TrailReviewComment struct {
	ID                        string                       `json:"id"`
	TrailID                   string                       `json:"trailId"`
	RepositoryID              string                       `json:"repositoryId"`
	ReviewID                  string                       `json:"reviewId"`
	CodeVersionID             string                       `json:"codeVersionId"`
	ActorID                   string                       `json:"actorId"`
	Title                     *string                      `json:"title"`
	Body                      *string                      `json:"body"`
	Severity                  *string                      `json:"severity"`
	Confidence                *float64                     `json:"confidence"`
	Status                    string                       `json:"status"`
	StatusReason              *string                      `json:"statusReason"`
	StaleOutcome              string                       `json:"staleOutcome"`
	StaleCheckedAt            *time.Time                   `json:"staleCheckedAt"`
	StaleCheckedCodeVersionID *string                      `json:"staleCheckedCodeVersionId"`
	ClientID                  *string                      `json:"clientId"`
	ClientIDHash              *string                      `json:"clientIdHash"`
	CreatedAt                 time.Time                    `json:"createdAt"`
	UpdatedAt                 time.Time                    `json:"updatedAt"`
	Location                  TrailReviewLocation          `json:"location"`
	SuggestedChanges          []TrailReviewSuggestedChange `json:"suggestedChanges,omitempty"`
	ThreadID                  *string                      `json:"threadId,omitempty"`
	ThreadMessageCount        int                          `json:"threadMessageCount,omitempty"`
	OutgoingLinks             []TrailReviewOutgoingLink    `json:"outgoingLinks,omitempty"`
}

Addressed in `6260342af` and pushed.

The query keys are intentional: entire-api review reads preserve BFF parity using `include_dismissed`, `limit`/`offset`, and snapshot `cursor`—not `pageSize`/`pageToken`.

I added:

- Contract comments and regression coverage.
- Repeated/empty-page detection so `fetchAllTrailReviewComments` cannot loop forever if a server violates the pagination contract.

`go test ./... -count=1` and lint pass.

Severity: medium

Selected context:
```
if author == "" {
```
In `listTrailResources`, when `author` is set the loop never breaks on `len(items) >= limit` (that check is gated behind `if author == ""`) — it only stops once `NextPageToken` is exhausted. Against entire-api's 100-row page cap, `entire trail list --author <login> -n 5` on a repo with a long trail history will walk every page of trails just to satisfy a small `--limit`, unlike the legacy path which filtered server-side in a single request. This is a real scalability regression for author-filtered listing under the entire-api backend.

content.text:
Fixed in `512908dc6` and pushed.

Author-filtered entire-api lists now stop as soon as `--limit` matching trails are collected instead of exhausting every cursor page. Added a regression test confirming `--author alice --limit 5` makes only one request when the first page satisfies the limit.

Full tests and lint pass.

Entire Trail review comment
ID: 019ff158-2c88-76de-9a31-0668edbd250f
URL: https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1008/migrate-trail-commands-to-entire-api
Severity: medium
Two normalizers in this PR; only the SSE one protects free-form data

`normalizeTrailEventValue` (`trail_watch_cmd.go`) deliberately exempts the free-form key so event data is not re-cased:

```go
if key == "payload" {
    out[key] = child
    continue
}
```

`normalizeTrailJSONValue` here has no equivalent guard — it re-cases every key at every depth, on both the read path (`decodeNormalizedTrailJSON`, used by ~13 UnmarshalJSON methods across trail/review/thread types) and the write path (`legacyTrailRequestBody`, which every request body on the **default** backend passes through).

Verified against this head (512908dc6):

```
read   {"id":"t1","context":{"my_custom_key":1},"labels":{"team_a":true}}
    -> {"id":"t1","context":{"myCustomKey":1},"labels":{"teamA":true}}

write  {"metadata":{"userDefinedKey":1,"already_snake":2}}
    -> {"metadata":{"user_defined_key":1,"already_snake":2}}
```

**Latent, not live:** no trail type currently declares a `map[string]any`; the only free-form field is `TrailApproval.Author` (`json.RawMessage`), and re-casing an author object is harmless. So nothing is corrupted today. Filing it because the same PR already recognises the hazard in the sibling normalizer, so the fix is known and cheap, and the first free-form field to land here (metadata, labels, annotations, a stored context blob) would be silently mangled in both directions with no test catching it.

Suggested fix: give `normalizeTrailJSONValue` the same treatment — either exempt known free-form keys as the SSE path does, or narrow re-casing to a schema key allowlist instead of walking arbitrary depth. A shared helper for both normalizers would also resolve the divergence noted separately (`snakeToLowerCamel` lacks `trailEventCamelKey`’s `reviewSessionId -> reviewId` remap, so `review_session_id` normalizes differently depending on which path handles it).
